steps.text: Deposit the US$250 minimum by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your risk settings, choose automatic or manual mode, and keep the demo running while you learn.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
cons: Marketing numbers that the fine print walks back.
No independent audit of the models.
Registration details not stated up front.
redFlags: Support figures that contradict each other.
Template placeholders left unrendered.
Return claims without verification.
The fee that is not a fee: spreads embedded in every trade.
The published score doubles as marketing copy with no methodology.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

bottomLine: The desk, the demo and the funding options all check out. The score reflects the paperwork around them.
Our 4.5 reflects what the pages publish and what they skip. It is not a warning off - it is a reminder to trade the product, not the pitch.
The CAUTION mark comes from disclosure gaps that a platform asking for deposits should not have.
